title: Example 125: a JWT skew moved from the window's ends to the clock, proved equal under the module's precondition by the tool's own checker
description: Runs build.py on example 125, a B9 regression proof on Crosscut's security.JwtTimestamps#valid with approach.engine native: now >= nbf - skew && now < exp + skew rewritten as now + skew >= nbf && now - skew < exp, with the module's precondition (from properties.contract) negated as intendedInputs. Inside the precondition no sum overflows and the versions agree; the tool's own checker (lib/src/bmc, CaDiCaL) proves it path by path. The library's run of this shape took 0.3 s over eleven paths. Without the scope the versions differ on an overflow near the range of a long, which the example's notes record.
expected: verdict verified; the proof line names jvmcontract's own checker (CaDiCaL) and the scope
